item.title: IP State 1.0.1
item.description:
## 💿 IP State 1.0.1

**Your public IP, at a glance.** This release adds a DMG download for drag-and-drop installation.

### ✨ What's new

- Add a styled universal DMG with an installation arrow, **IP State.app**, and an **Applications** shortcut.
- Offer SHA-256 checksums for both downloads.
- Keep the signed ZIP for automatic app updates.

### ⬇️ Install or update

Download **IPState-1.0.1-universal-macos.dmg**. Open it and drag **IP State.app** onto **Applications**.
Eject the disk image, then open **IP State** from Applications.
You can also download the ZIP, extract it, and move the app into Applications.
Both downloads support Apple silicon and Intel and require macOS 14 or later.

Already on 0.11.0 or later? Choose **Check for Updates…** in the app menu.
Earlier versions need one manual installation to enable app updates.
Your existing IP State settings remain intact.

### ℹ️ First launch

This release is ad-hoc signed and **not notarized by Apple**. macOS may block its first launch.
See [Apple's instructions for opening an unidentified developer's app](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mh40617/mac).
The source is available if you prefer to build it yourself.

Each `.sha256` file records the checksum of its corresponding download.
Sparkle verifies the ZIP update archive's signature before installation.

item.title: IP State 1.0.0
item.description:
## 🌍 IP State 1.0

**Your public IP, at a glance.** IP State's first stable release keeps your VPN's exit IP, location, and connection status in the macOS menu bar.

### ✨ What's included

- Show your public IP, country flag, country code, city, or a combination. Reorder items and limit long names.
- Track IPv4 and IPv6 independently, with automatic selection for the menu bar.
- Check on network changes and wake, plus a configurable interval from five seconds to 15 minutes.
- Get IP-change alerts with the full address and available location. Enable optional connection loss and recovery alerts.
- Reuse remembered IP locations and opt into local history with a configurable limit.
- Check for signed app updates manually or daily. Preview releases are optional; installation requires confirmation.

### ⬇️ Install or update

Download **IPState-1.0.0-universal-macos.zip**, extract it, and move **IP State.app** into Applications.
The universal app supports Apple silicon and Intel and requires macOS 14 or later.

Already on 0.11.0? Choose **Check for Updates…** in the app menu.
Earlier versions need one manual installation to enable app updates.
Your existing IP State settings remain intact.

### ℹ️ First launch

This release is ad-hoc signed and **not notarized by Apple**. macOS may block its first launch.
See [Apple's instructions for opening an unidentified developer's app](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mh40617/mac).

item.title: IP State 0.11.0
item.description:
IP State shows your public IP and location in the macOS menu bar and alerts you when the address changes.

Version 0.11.0 adds **Check for Updates…** to the menu and native, signed app updates through Sparkle.
Settings offers optional daily update checks and an opt-in preview channel. Installation always requires confirmation.
Existing versions have no updater: install this build manually once to receive future updates from the app.
Your existing IP State settings remain intact.

The default menu bar shows a country flag and code. Public IP checks continue independently of location lookup.
VPN changes reset retry delays, and canceled IP alerts stay canceled when notifications are re-enabled.
Recent IP locations are remembered across restarts, with automatic revalidation and expiry.

Download the universal macOS ZIP for Apple silicon or Intel, extract it, and move **IP State.app** into Applications.
Requires macOS 14 or later.

This preview is ad-hoc signed and **not notarized by Apple**. macOS may block its first launch.
See [Apple's instructions for opening an unidentified developer's app](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mh40617/mac).
The source is available if you prefer to build it yourself.

The `.sha256` file records the ZIP's SHA-256 checksum.
